# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which specifies that the wire to cut depends on the color of the cycling light at the moment of the cut (red -> yellow, white -> green, yellow -> blue). 

However, this is Turn 1. I cannot speak; I can only gesture to Deaf. Without an established sign system between Deaf and myself, any gesture I make right now carries no shared meaning. Furthermore, Deaf has not yet observed the bomb to report its state or propose an encoding, and Blind cannot see gestures at all.

I will wait for Deaf to observe the bomb and speak, so we can establish a protocol and coordinate the cut.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2

moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |

| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I can cut wire 1, 2, or 3. Deaf goes next and cannot hear us. When Deaf describes the bomb, check the manual and gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Deaf can then speak that wire number aloud so I can cut it.
Deaf says: Bomb state: Display shows 0. Light is blue. Wires are: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is yellow. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.

I hold the defusal manual. The manual states:
- The light changes every round, walking a circle of five colours.
- What matters is the light color at the moment of the cut:
  - Red light -> cut yellow wire (Wire 3)
  - White light -> cut green wire (Wire 2)
  - Yellow light -> cut blue wire (Wire 1)

In Round 1, Deaf observed the light was blue (which has no valid cut condition in the manual). Furthermore, the light changes every round, and Blind acts before Deaf in each round, meaning Blind cannot cut blindly until we track the light cycle and timing. 

I must instruct Deaf and Blind to hold/wait so Deaf can observe and report the next light color in the cycle. I am gesturing ✋ (stop / wait) to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Light is now yellow. Display is 0. Wires: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute gestured ✋. Mute, if you need a wire cut or button pressed, please gesture ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 3 for 3, or clarify what ✋ means.

I need to observe the light cycle to know what color will be active when Blind performs the cut. The light was Blue in Round 1 and Yellow in Round 2. Since Blind cuts before Deaf observes in each round, any instruction given now would take effect in Round 4, whose color is currently unknown. To avoid detonating the bomb on an incorrect light state, I will wait and let Deaf observe and report the next color in the sequence.

```

```

Deaf says: Update: Light is now RED. Display is still 0. Wires are still: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute sent no gestures this turn.

If finger emojis don't work, send thumbs up 👍 for 1, peace ✌ for 2, or open hand 🖐 for 3.
Deaf says: Status update Turn 4: Light is now WHITE. (Light history: T1 blue, T2 yellow, T3 red, T4 white). Display remains 0. Wires remain: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, remember I cannot hear Blind; please gesture to me any instructions or answers to relay.

I am waiting this round so that the five-colour light cycle completes its first full rotation. By waiting in Turn 5 and sending the signal in Turn 6, Deaf will relay the instruction at the end of Turn 6, allowing Blind to cut wire 1 during Turn 7 exactly when the light returns to yellow.

Blind says to Mute: Mute: The emojis you send might be rendering as '?' on Deaf's screen. To be completely unambiguous, use the COUNT of symbols: send 1 gesture for wire 1 (e.g. ['👍']), 2 gestures for wire 2 (e.g. ['👍', '👍']), or 3 gestures for wire 3 (e.g. ['👍', '👍', '👍']). Bomb status: Light is now WHITE (history: blue, yellow, red, white), display is 0, wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please gesture to Deaf now with 1, 2, or 3 symbols so Deaf can speak the wire number to me.
Deaf says: Turn 5: Light is now GREEN. History: blue -> yellow -> red -> white -> green. Display: 0. Wires: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, please gesture instructions if Blind needs to do something!

The full 5-color cycle has now completed:
Round 1: blue
Round 2: yellow
Round 3: red
Round 4: white
Round 5: green

In Round 6:
- Light will be blue.
- In Turn 6, I gesture to Deaf. Deaf receives it at the end of Turn 6 and speaks to Blind.

In Round 7:
- Blind acts at the start of Turn 7.
- The light in Round 7 will be yellow (following the cycle: blue -> yellow).
- According to the defusal manual:
  "yellow light -> cut blue wire"
- Wire 1 is blue.
- Blind and Deaf agreed on wire indexing where 1 symbol / ☝ means wire 1.
- Therefore, in Round 7, when the light is yellow, Blind must cut wire 1.

I gesture `☝` to Deaf so Deaf will speak to Blind to cut wire 1 in Round 7.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Deaf says: Turn 6 update: Light is BLUE. Display: 0. Mute just gestured: [☝] (One). Blind, Mute is signalling number 1 (wire 1 or option 1). If you asked a question, the answer is 1.

I have already conveyed the instruction (wire 1) through Deaf, and Blind will act on it in this round (Turn 7). During Turn 7, the light is yellow, which according to the manual requires cutting the blue wire (wire 1). Everything is aligned.

